description:
The housing stock and what it costs: total units and the vacancy rate ([B25002](https://data.census.gov/table/ACSDT5Y2024.B25002)), households and the owner-occupied share ([B25003](https://data.census.gov/table/ACSDT5Y2024.B25003)), median gross rent ([B25064](https://data.census.gov/table/ACSDT5Y2024.B25064)) and median owner-occupied home value ([B25077](https://data.census.gov/table/ACSDT5Y2024.B25077)), the share of renter households paying 30% and 50% or more of income on rent ([B25070](https://data.census.gov/table/ACSDT5Y2024.B25070)), the pre-1940 share ([B25034](https://data.census.gov/table/ACSDT5Y2024.B25034)) and the single-family share ([B25024](https://data.census.gov/table/ACSDT5Y2024.B25024)).

Curated indicators for all **3,235** counties and county equivalents in the United States, Puerto Rico and the island areas, from the U.S. Census Bureau's [American Community Survey](https://www.census.gov/programs-surveys/acs.html) **2020–2024 5-year estimates** (`acsdt5y2024`, the table-based [Summary File](https://www2.census.gov/programs-surveys/acs/summary_file/2024/table-based-SF/data/5YRData/)). The Census Bureau calls the ACS "the premier source of detailed information about the nation's people and housing". The Bureau also publishes 1-year estimates at this geography; the 5-year release is used throughout this catalog so every geography in it is the same vintage and directly comparable.

Every estimate ships with its margin of error — `<column>_moe`, at the 90% confidence level, the level the Census Bureau publishes — and the headline statistics also carry a coefficient of variation (`<column>_cv` = `moe / 1.645 / estimate`) so small-area noise can be flagged rather than mapped as if certain. Derived percentages propagate error with the Census Bureau's own formulas from [ACS Accuracy of the Data](https://www2.census.gov/programs-surveys/acs/tech_docs/accuracy/MultiyearACSAccuracyofData2024.pdf): sums add in quadrature, proportions use the subset formula with the ratio formula as fallback. ACS jam values for suppressed or unestimable cells are NULL here, never numbers, and medians are published as the Bureau publishes them — a median cannot be aggregated to a larger area. Each column's description names its ACS table, its exact universe, and the lines summed to make it.

Counties are the coarsest geography most questions are actually asked at, and the most reliable in this catalog below state level: the median coefficient of variation on `median_hh_income` is **0.042** here against 0.125 at tract level (measured). One context column breaks the catalog's own rule — `population_moe` is NULL on **3,103 of the 3,235 rows**, only 132 small rural counties carrying a margin on `population` — so read `population` here as a count to use rather than an estimate to put an interval on. `median_gross_rent` is NULL on **0.62%** of counties and `median_home_value` on **0.56%** — against 5.92% and 3.55% at tract level and 29.68% and 10.03% at block group.

Geometries are the Census Bureau's [2024 cartographic boundary files](https://www.census.gov/geographies/mapping-files/time-series/geo/cartographic-boundary.html) for counties and county equivalents (GENZ2024, 1:500,000), reprojected to EPSG:4326 and joined on `GEOID`. Cartographic rather than TIGER/Line because TIGER extends census geographies into open water while the cartographic files clip to the shoreline, which is what a choropleth wants. The boundary vintage matches the estimate vintage.

The join is driven by geometry, so a geography with 2024 boundaries but no ACS tabulation keeps its row with NULL values instead of disappearing: 13 county equivalents in the island areas, which have cartographic boundaries but no ACS 5-year estimates because the Island Areas run a separate decennial-only program. Keeping these rows means a national map has no holes and a consumer can see the absence; dropping them would make "every US geography" quietly mean something narrower.

This is one themed chunk of six at this geography. The other themes are [Income & Poverty](../county-income/collection.json), [People & Education](../county-people/collection.json), [Commuting & Connectivity](../county-connectivity/collection.json) and [Health, Disability & Income by Race](../county-wellbeing/collection.json), split that way so a consumer who wants one theme reads one file. Chunks at the same geography hold the same rows and the same geometry, so they join 1:1 on `geoid`. A sixth collection, [All Indicators](../counties/collection.json), carries all 135 columns on the same rows in one wide table — at this many features width costs little, so take that one if a question crosses themes. GEOIDs nest by prefix: `substr(geoid, 1, 2)` is the state, and tracts and block groups join back on their own first 5 characters. Every other geography in this catalog is organized the same way — [block groups](../../block-groups/catalog.json), [census tracts](../../tracts/catalog.json), [states](../../states/catalog.json), [ZCTAs](../../zctas/catalog.json), [places and CDPs](../../places/catalog.json) and [congressional districts](../../congressional-districts/catalog.json) — and the [blocks](../../blocks/collection.json) collection carries 2020 Decennial counts, a different survey and vintage rather than a finer version of these numbers.

The PMTiles archive carries the same columns as the GeoParquet, minus the `*_moe` columns, and at every zoom the tiles are the real census geographies — there are few enough features here to draw them all at a national zoom, so this archive needs none of the coarser-geography coarse-zoom bands the catalog's finer collections carry. Built with [tylertoo](https://github.com/geoparquet-io/tylertoo). Statistics still come from the GeoParquet: margins of error are not in the tiles.

This is a mirror — [data.census.gov](https://data.census.gov/) is authoritative, and nothing here is an official Census Bureau product. The exact upstream files this collection was built from are published as `source` assets, linked at their original census.gov URLs, so the original is always one click away; the Bureau's own documentation is linked alongside them. Read the collection's [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) before querying: it carries the schema, the join keys, the NULL-rate story and tested queries against the published URLs.

table:columns.name: geoid
table:columns.description: 5-character county (or county-equivalent) GEOID — state (2) + county (3), e.g. `29510` for St. Louis city. Includes Puerto Rico municipios and the island-area county equivalents. Matches `GEOID` in the 2024 cartographic boundary county file; the ACS `0500000US` prefix is stripped.

table:columns.name: name
table:columns.description: Human-readable name from the cartographic boundary county file: `NAMELSAD`, `STATE_NAME` — "St. Louis city, Missouri".

table:columns.name: state
table:columns.description: Two-letter USPS state or territory code (`MO`, `PR`, `GU`). Carried on every collection from the `STATEFP → USPS` lookup embedded in `tools/specs.py` rather than read off the boundary files, because the 2024 cartographic boundary block-group file has no `STUSPS` column while the tract, county and state files do.

table:columns.name: population
table:columns.description: Total population. Universe: total population. The single line of [B01003](https://data.census.gov/table/ACSDT5Y2024.B01003) (Total Population), published as an integer. Carried on every ACS collection so a rate can be weighted or sanity-checked without a second download. NULL on 0.40% of counties — the 13 island-area county equivalents (AS 5, GU 1, MP 4, VI 3), which have cartographic boundaries but no ACS 5-year estimates.

table:columns.name: population_moe
table:columns.description: Margin of error for `population` at the 90% confidence level, the level the Census Bureau publishes. Component margins add in quadrature — `sqrt(Σ moe²)` — which is the Census Bureau's formula for the margin of a sum. NULL when every component is a jam value.

table:columns.name: aland_sqkm
table:columns.description: Land area in square kilometres, rounded to 3 decimals. `ALAND / 1e6` from the cartographic boundary file. Land only: water area is excluded, which is what makes it the right denominator for population density.

table:columns.name: pop_density
table:columns.description: People per square kilometre of land area, rounded to 1 decimal: `population / aland_sqkm`. NULL where `ALAND` is 0 or `population` is NULL.

table:columns.name: housing_units
table:columns.description: Total housing units, occupied and vacant. Universe: housing units. Line 1 of [B25002](https://data.census.gov/table/ACSDT5Y2024.B25002) (Occupancy Status), published as an integer.

table:columns.name: housing_units_moe
table:columns.description: Margin of error for `housing_units` at the 90% confidence level, the level the Census Bureau publishes. Component margins add in quadrature — `sqrt(Σ moe²)` — which is the Census Bureau's formula for the margin of a sum. NULL when every component is a jam value.

table:columns.name: pct_vacant_units
table:columns.description: Percent of housing units that are vacant. Universe: housing units. Line 3 ("Vacant") over line 1 of [B25002](https://data.census.gov/table/ACSDT5Y2024.B25002). The ACS counts for-sale, for-rent, seasonal and migrant-worker units as vacant, so this is not a measure of abandonment.

table:columns.name: pct_vacant_units_moe
table:columns.description: Margin of error for `pct_vacant_units` at the 90% confidence level, the level the Census Bureau publishes. Propagated with the Census Bureau's proportion formula, `sqrt(moe_num² − p²·moe_den²) / den`, falling back to the ratio formula (`+` instead of `−`) when the radicand goes negative because the numerator is not a true subset of the denominator. Multiplied by 100 to match the percentage, rounded to 2 decimals, and NULL rather than guessed when an input margin is NULL or the denominator is 0.

table:columns.name: households
table:columns.description: Households — occupied housing units. One household per occupied unit, by definition. Universe: occupied housing units. Line 1 of [B25003](https://data.census.gov/table/ACSDT5Y2024.B25003) (Tenure), published as an integer.

table:columns.name: households_moe
table:columns.description: Margin of error for `households` at the 90% confidence level, the level the Census Bureau publishes. Component margins add in quadrature — `sqrt(Σ moe²)` — which is the Census Bureau's formula for the margin of a sum. NULL when every component is a jam value.

table:columns.name: pct_owner_occupied
table:columns.description: Percent of occupied housing units that are owner-occupied. Universe: occupied housing units. Line 2 ("Owner occupied") over line 1 of [B25003](https://data.census.gov/table/ACSDT5Y2024.B25003). The homeownership rate of households, not of people, and vacant units are outside the universe entirely.

table:columns.name: pct_owner_occupied_moe
table:columns.description: Margin of error for `pct_owner_occupied` at the 90% confidence level, the level the Census Bureau publishes. Propagated with the Census Bureau's proportion formula, `sqrt(moe_num² − p²·moe_den²) / den`, falling back to the ratio formula (`+` instead of `−`) when the radicand goes negative because the numerator is not a true subset of the denominator. Multiplied by 100 to match the percentage, rounded to 2 decimals, and NULL rather than guessed when an input margin is NULL or the denominator is 0.

table:columns.name: median_gross_rent
table:columns.description: Median gross rent in dollars per month — contract rent plus the estimated average monthly cost of utilities and fuels. Universe: renter-occupied housing units **paying cash rent**, so units occupied rent-free are excluded. Line 1 of [B25064](https://data.census.gov/table/ACSDT5Y2024.B25064).

table:columns.name: median_gross_rent_moe
table:columns.description: Margin of error for `median_gross_rent` at the 90% confidence level, the level the Census Bureau publishes. Published as the Census Bureau publishes it for this line. A median's margin cannot be recomputed from a distribution, so it is passed through untouched.

table:columns.name: median_gross_rent_cv
table:columns.description: Coefficient of variation for `median_gross_rent`: `moe / 1.645 / estimate`, rounded to 3 decimals — the standard error as a fraction of the estimate, with 1.645 converting the published 90% margin back to a standard error. A rule of thumb: under 0.12 reliable, 0.12–0.40 use with caution, over 0.40 unreliable. NULL when the estimate is NULL or 0, or the margin of error is NULL. Published on the headline statistics so a map can grey out the geographies whose value is swamped by its own error instead of drawing them as if certain.

table:columns.name: pct_rent_burdened
table:columns.description: Percent of renter households paying 30% or more of household income on gross rent — the standard affordability threshold. Universe: renter-occupied housing units, less those whose ratio the Census could not compute. Lines 7–10 (30.0–34.9, 35.0–39.9, 40.0–49.9, 50.0 percent or more) of [B25070](https://data.census.gov/table/ACSDT5Y2024.B25070) over line 1 minus line 11 ("Not computed" — no cash rent, or no income). Including the not-computed units in the denominator would understate the burden.

table:columns.name: pct_rent_burdened_moe
table:columns.description: Margin of error for `pct_rent_burdened` at the 90% confidence level, the level the Census Bureau publishes. Propagated with the Census Bureau's proportion formula, `sqrt(moe_num² − p²·moe_den²) / den`, falling back to the ratio formula (`+` instead of `−`) when the radicand goes negative because the numerator is not a true subset of the denominator. Multiplied by 100 to match the percentage, rounded to 2 decimals, and NULL rather than guessed when an input margin is NULL or the denominator is 0.

table:columns.name: pct_rent_burdened_cv
table:columns.description: Coefficient of variation for `pct_rent_burdened`: `moe / 1.645 / estimate`, rounded to 3 decimals — the standard error as a fraction of the estimate, with 1.645 converting the published 90% margin back to a standard error. A rule of thumb: under 0.12 reliable, 0.12–0.40 use with caution, over 0.40 unreliable. NULL when the estimate is NULL or 0, or the margin of error is NULL. Published on the headline statistics so a map can grey out the geographies whose value is swamped by its own error instead of drawing them as if certain.

table:columns.name: pct_severely_rent_burdened
table:columns.description: Percent of renter households paying 50% or more of household income on gross rent. Universe: renter-occupied housing units, less those whose ratio could not be computed. Line 10 of [B25070](https://data.census.gov/table/ACSDT5Y2024.B25070) over line 1 minus line 11. A subset of `pct_rent_burdened`.

table:columns.name: pct_severely_rent_burdened_moe
table:columns.description: Margin of error for `pct_severely_rent_burdened` at the 90% confidence level, the level the Census Bureau publishes. Propagated with the Census Bureau's proportion formula, `sqrt(moe_num² − p²·moe_den²) / den`, falling back to the ratio formula (`+` instead of `−`) when the radicand goes negative because the numerator is not a true subset of the denominator. Multiplied by 100 to match the percentage, rounded to 2 decimals, and NULL rather than guessed when an input margin is NULL or the denominator is 0.

table:columns.name: median_home_value
table:columns.description: Median value of owner-occupied housing units, in dollars — the owner's estimate of what the property would sell for, not an assessment or a sale price. Universe: owner-occupied housing units. Line 1 of [B25077](https://data.census.gov/table/ACSDT5Y2024.B25077).

table:columns.name: median_home_value_moe
table:columns.description: Margin of error for `median_home_value` at the 90% confidence level, the level the Census Bureau publishes. Published as the Census Bureau publishes it for this line. A median's margin cannot be recomputed from a distribution, so it is passed through untouched.

table:columns.name: median_home_value_cv
table:columns.description: Coefficient of variation for `median_home_value`: `moe / 1.645 / estimate`, rounded to 3 decimals — the standard error as a fraction of the estimate, with 1.645 converting the published 90% margin back to a standard error. A rule of thumb: under 0.12 reliable, 0.12–0.40 use with caution, over 0.40 unreliable. NULL when the estimate is NULL or 0, or the margin of error is NULL. Published on the headline statistics so a map can grey out the geographies whose value is swamped by its own error instead of drawing them as if certain.

table:columns.name: pct_built_pre_1940
table:columns.description: Percent of housing units built in 1939 or earlier. Universe: housing units. Line 11 of [B25034](https://data.census.gov/table/ACSDT5Y2024.B25034) (Year Structure Built) over line 1. The oldest bucket the table publishes, and a standard screening proxy for lead-paint risk.

table:columns.name: pct_built_pre_1940_moe
table:columns.description: Margin of error for `pct_built_pre_1940` at the 90% confidence level, the level the Census Bureau publishes. Propagated with the Census Bureau's proportion formula, `sqrt(moe_num² − p²·moe_den²) / den`, falling back to the ratio formula (`+` instead of `−`) when the radicand goes negative because the numerator is not a true subset of the denominator. Multiplied by 100 to match the percentage, rounded to 2 decimals, and NULL rather than guessed when an input margin is NULL or the denominator is 0.

table:columns.name: pct_single_family
table:columns.description: Percent of housing units in single-family structures. Universe: housing units. Lines 2 ("1, detached") + 3 ("1, attached") over line 1 of [B25024](https://data.census.gov/table/ACSDT5Y2024.B25024) (Units in Structure). Attached single-family — rowhouses, townhouses — is included; a duplex (line 4) is not.

table:columns.name: pct_single_family_moe
table:columns.description: Margin of error for `pct_single_family` at the 90% confidence level, the level the Census Bureau publishes. Propagated with the Census Bureau's proportion formula, `sqrt(moe_num² − p²·moe_den²) / den`, falling back to the ratio formula (`+` instead of `−`) when the radicand goes negative because the numerator is not a true subset of the denominator. Multiplied by 100 to match the percentage, rounded to 2 decimals, and NULL rather than guessed when an input margin is NULL or the denominator is 0.

table:columns.name: geometry
table:columns.description: Boundary polygon (Polygon or MultiPolygon), WKB-encoded, in EPSG:4326 / OGC:CRS84 — the GeoParquet default CRS, written as an omitted `crs` key. From the Census Bureau's 2024 cartographic boundary county file (GENZ2024, 1:500,000), which clips to the shoreline — TIGER/Line would extend the county into open water. Generalized for mapping and point-in-polygon work, not for legal-boundary or precise-area work.

table:columns.name: bbox
table:columns.type: struct<xmin: double, ymin: double, xmax: double, ymax: double>
table:columns.description: GeoParquet 1.1 covering struct (`xmin`, `ymin`, `xmax`, `ymax`) for the row's geometry, with row-group statistics, so a spatial filter can skip most of the file over the network. Written by geoparquet-io, not by the Census Bureau.

title: Housing & Rent — Counties

providers.name: U.S. Census Bureau
providers.description: Produces the American Community Survey, the Decennial Census, and the TIGER/cartographic boundary geographies this catalog is built from.

providers.name: Portolan Mirrors
providers.description: Converted the published summary files and boundary files to cloud-native formats and maintains this mirror. Not an official Census Bureau product.

styles/default.title: Median home value
styles/default.description: Median value of owner-occupied homes, pale amber to burnt brown. Measured over all 3,217 counties with a published value: 7 classes with breaks at $110k/$150k/$200k/$275k/$400k/$650k, which fall at the 11th/30th/56th/76th/91st/98th percentile of the national distribution. 0.5% have a coefficient of variation above 0.3 and render faded — the estimate is real but its margin of error swamps it.

styles/ownership.title: Owner-occupied homes
styles/ownership.description: Share of occupied housing units lived in by their owner, pale to deep green. Measured over all 3,222 counties with a published value: 7 classes with breaks at 62%/70%/75%/78%/82%/85%, which fall at the 10th/29th/52nd/70th/89th/96th percentile of the national distribution.

styles/pre-1940.title: Homes built before 1940
styles/pre-1940.description: Share of housing units built in 1939 or earlier, pale parchment to dark sepia. Measured over all 3,222 counties with a published value: 6 classes with breaks at 4%/7.5%/14%/23%/32%, which fall at the 19th/40th/60th/79th/92nd percentile of the national distribution.

styles/rent-burden.title: Renters paying 30%+ of income
styles/rent-burden.description: Share of renter households spending 30% or more of income on gross rent — the federal definition of rent-burdened — pale mauve to deep magenta. Measured over all 3,222 counties with a published value: 7 classes with breaks at 30%/40%/45%/50%/55%/58%, which fall at the 9th/29th/51st/72nd/89th/95th percentile of the national distribution. 7.85% have a coefficient of variation above 0.3 and render faded — the estimate is real but its margin of error swamps it.

styles/vacancy.title: Vacant housing units
styles/vacancy.description: Share of housing units vacant, cream to dark red; seasonal and recreational housing drives the high end as much as abandonment does. Measured over all 3,222 counties with a published value: 6 classes with breaks at 8%/12%/16%/22%/30%, which fall at the 19th/39th/58th/78th/91st percentile of the national distribution.

source-table-shells.title: ACS 2020–2024 5-year table shells
source-table-shells.description: `Table ID|Line|Indent|Unique ID|Label|Title|Universe|Type` for every table in the release. Two jobs here: every line number the build reads is pinned against this file and a vintage that renumbers a line fails the build, and every universe quoted in the column descriptions is this file's own `Universe` field. Served by census.gov.

source-cartographic-boundaries.title: 2024 cartographic boundary file — counties and county equivalents (1:500,000, national)
source-cartographic-boundaries.description: The geometry this collection joins onto, shoreline-clipped and generalized for mapping. Only the join key, the name parts and the land-area field are kept; reprojected from NAD83 to EPSG:4326 with ogr2ogr. Served by census.gov.

doc-acs-handbook.title: Understanding and Using American Community Survey Data — Census Bureau handbooks
doc-acs-handbook.description: The Bureau's own guidance on what ACS estimates can and cannot support: 1-year versus 5-year releases, margins of error, comparing across vintages, and small-area reliability. Read it before drawing a conclusion from a single block group.

doc-acs-accuracy.title: ACS Accuracy of the Data (2024, multiyear estimates)
doc-acs-accuracy.description: The source of every margin-of-error formula this build applies: quadrature for sums, the proportion formula and its ratio fallback for percentages, and the definition of the published 90% confidence level.

doc-acs-subject-definitions.title: ACS 2024 Subject Definitions
doc-acs-subject-definitions.description: The Census Bureau's definitions of the concepts behind these columns — household, householder, gross rent, poverty status determined, group quarters, means of transportation to work, disability. Where a column description here says what a universe is, this is the document it is saying it from.

doc-geo-glossary.title: Census Bureau geography program glossary
doc-geo-glossary.description: Definitions of the geographies and the identifiers used here — block, block group, tract, county equivalent, GEOID, and what nests inside what.
